newsitem.title: EGYPT: EU draws applause with Mideast land-for-peace plea.
newsitem.headline: EU draws applause with Mideast land-for-peace plea.

text.p: The European Union (EU) drew long applause from mainly Arab businessmen at the Middle East economic conference in Cairo on Tuesday when it said that land-for-peace must be the basis of a Middle East settlement.
Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, whose country chairs the EU for this six-month period, described the stalemate in peace talks as a crisis of deep concern to Europe.
"The European Union is more than ever convinced that peace in the Middle East depends on the full implementation of the existing agreements between Israel and the Palestinians.

"I would like to take this opportunity to appeal to the parties...to reclaim the spirit of Madrid and Oslo and to continue towards the common goal of a lasting, just and comprehensive peace for the full region on the basis of all relevant resolutions of the United Nations Security Council and the principle of land for peace," he said.

The new Israeli government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, which took office in June, has angered Israel's Arab neighbours by questioning the need for Israel to give up any more Arab territory, such as the Golan Heights to Syria.
Land-for-peace was part of the framework for the Middle East peace conference held in Madrid in 1991 and the previous Israeli government was committed to the principle.

Spring, who has just ended a tour of the Middle East, also drew applause when he spoke about the economic plight of the Palestinians, who complain that Israeli policies such as border closures are crippling their economy.
"It is of vital importance that the Palestinian people see the economic benefits of peace and this should happen without any further delay," he said.
Spring said on Monday he wanted Israel to ease border restrictions, allow the Palestinians to build a port in Gaza and give them easier access to Gaza's airfield.
